findings.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md checklist shows only 'Reproduce + root-cause' checked; the rest ('Add plugin', 'Wire it into preview.ts', 'Unit tests', 'Note deviation', 'Draft PR') are unchecked, yet the filename date (20260724) is a month before today (2026-08-24). This is only a minor naming/timeline inconsistency, not a functional problem.

findings.summary: wrappedList's silent short-circuit skips upstream `list`'s ≥4-space indent guard
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (line 32) and never the upper bound `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` that markdown-it's own `list` rule applies first. The wrapper (lines 182-191) returns `true` before delegating, so a 4+-space-indented lone `-` after a paragraph (`foo\n -`) would terminate the paragraph and then be re-tokenized by the `code` rule as an indented code block instead of staying a lazy continuation (`

foo
-

`). Mitigation I could not fully rule out: both callers of the 'paragraph' terminator chain (markdown-it's `paragraph` rule and the ported `lheading` at line 86) `continue` for lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3`, which may make this unreachable in practice — node_modules is absent in this worktree so I could not confirm the paragraph rule's source. Adding the same `>= 4` bail to `isEmptyBulletLine` is cheap insurance.

findings.summary: Paragraph-interrupt relaxation applies to `*` and `+` too, changing rendering beyond the documented lone-`-` case
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts 0x2a (`*`) and 0x2b (`+`) as well as `-` (line 39), so `wrappedList` now lets any empty bullet interrupt a paragraph. Upstream and the design doc (docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299, which scopes the deviation to a "lone single `-`") would render e.g. `1 + 2\n+` or `a\n*` as lazy continuation text `

a
*

`; with this plugin they become `

a

`. No test covers the `*`/`+` shapes, and the trailing-`*` case is plausible in prose (footnote markers, emphasis typos).

findings.summary: Re-implemented `asciiTrim` may not match upstream lheading's content trimming for non-ASCII whitespace
findings.evidence: Line 134 trims setext heading content with the local `ASCII_TRIM_RE` (space/\t/\n/\v/\f/\r only). markdown-it 14.x's `rules_block/lheading` trims the content with JS `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips NBSP ( ), ﻿ and Unicode spaces. If so, a heading like ` Heading\n===` now keeps the leading NBSP in the rendered `<h1>` where it previously did not. Cosmetic, but it is an unintended divergence in a rule described as a faithful port. Could not verify upstream source directly (no node_modules in the worktree).

findings.summary: getRuleFn reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throws at module-evaluation time if the shape changes
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` (lines 207-214) casts `md.block.ruler` to an object with a private `__rules__` array and throws `markdown-it block rule not found: list` if it is absent or renamed. It is called from `listEmptyBulletPlugin`, which `preview.ts:48` invokes at module top level, so any markdown-it internal rename (a patch/minor bump is enough — `markdown-it: ^14.1.0` in packages/notes/package.json floats) turns into an import-time exception that takes down the whole notes preview module, not just the bullet feature. A defensive fallback (skip the wrapper, leave stock `list` in place) would degrade instead of crash.

findings.summary: Single-dash setext headings (`Heading\n-`) no longer render as `<h2>` anywhere in notes
findings.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` (line 105) suppresses the setext underline unconditionally, not only when the line sits under a list item. Combined with the relaxed `list` rule, plain prose `Heading\n-` now renders as `

Heading

` where CommonMark/GitHub give `

Heading

`. The design doc records the deviation only for the nested-bullet shape (notes.md:293-299) and the tests only assert the multi-dash `---` case still works, so this wider regression is untested and undocumented.

findings.summary: Upstream markdown-it `lheading` rule is copy-forked wholesale instead of reused/wrapped
findings.evidence: `lheadingRule` re-implements markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` verbatim (terminator loop, token pushes, `asciiTrim` re-created at lines 17-22) for the sake of one added `isLoneDash` guard, and installs it with `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)`. The same file already demonstrates the cheaper reuse pattern for `list` (`getRuleFn` + delegate), so the fork is avoidable: the plugin could delegate to the original `lheading` and only pre-empt it when the underline candidate is a lone `-`. As written, any markdown-it upgrade silently keeps the frozen 14.x copy (including the private `asciiTrim` semantics) with nothing in CI to detect the drift.

findings.summary: Fix is broader than the issue: a lone single `-` is disqualified as a setext underline everywhere, not just under a list item
findings.evidence: The issue #517 outcome is scoped to "a list item followed by an empty nested list item" — the parent should keep body styling and the bullet nest as an empty child. The implemented guard `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` applies at every paragraph in the document, so top-level valid CommonMark setext headings written as `Title\n-` stop rendering as `<h2>` even though no list is involved. Likewise the `list` wrapper (lines 176-195) lets *any* empty bullet interrupt *any* paragraph. This is documented as deliberate in docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299, but it is a global markdown-semantics change delivered under a nested-list bug, i.e. unrequested scope beyond the acceptance criteria.

findings.summary: Depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: Array<{name; fn; enabled}> }` to recover the stock `list` rule. This couples the notes preview to a private, untyped library internal; a markdown-it internal rename turns into a runtime throw (`markdown-it block rule not found: list`) at module init rather than a type error. A public-API alternative (e.g. capturing the rule via a probe instance, or inserting a terminator rule `before('list')` rather than wrapping it) would avoid reaching into internals; the existing `details-plugin.ts` sticks to `ruler.before`.

findings.summary: Design doc records the deviation but not the collateral top-level `Title\n-` behavior change
findings.evidence: The new section is correctly folded into the canonical subsystem doc (no parallel file) and follows the `details-plugin` precedent, and the backticked path resolves. It does state multi-dash `---` and `=` underlines are untouched, but it does not call out that a *single*-dash setext underline at top level (`Title\n-`) now also stops being a heading — the most user-visible collateral of the deviation.

findings.summary: No test for the top-level `paragraph\n-` case, the most visible behavior change of the lheading rewrite
findings.evidence: The plugin's rewritten `lheading` rule (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105) refuses to treat a lone single `-` as a setext underline anywhere, not just inside a list. That means plain `Heading\n-` (valid CommonMark `<h2>`) now renders as a paragraph plus an empty list — a deliberate CommonMark deviation for all note content. The only setext test added is `preserves multi-dash setext headings` with `'Heading\n---'` (preview.test.ts:182-187), which exercises the untouched multi-dash path. Nothing pins down (or even documents in a test) what a lone top-level `-` now produces, so a future change to that guard cannot be detected.

findings.summary: Empty `*` and `+` bullets accepted by isEmptyBulletLine have no test
findings.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` explicitly accepts `-`, `*` and `+` markers (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:41-44), so the paragraph-terminating branch fires for `- 1\n  *` and `- 1\n  +` too. Every added test uses only `-` (preview.test.ts:155/170/177/191). The `*`/`+` branches of the new predicate are never exercised, so a regression there is invisible.
searchedFor: grep for `render\(` in packages/notes/src to enumerate all markdown fixtures

findings.summary: The rewritten lheading rule's `=` (h1) branch is not covered anywhere
findings.evidence: The whole upstream lheading rule was re-implemented, including the `marker === EQUALS -> level 1` path (line 108), the `asciiTrim` content extraction and the token map/markup assignments. No test renders `Heading\n===`; the only h1 assertion in the package (editor.test.ts:17) comes from ATX `# Title`, not setext. A copy error in the `=` path would ship green.

findings.summary: Two of the new tests assert only structure existence, not that the nested item is the empty bullet
findings.evidence: `nests an empty bullet with a trailing space too` (line 168-173) and `still renders the blank-line workaround correctly` (line 175-180) assert only `querySelector('ul > li > ul > li')` is truthy plus no `h2`. They would pass equally if the nested item contained arbitrary text (e.g. if the marker leaked through as content), unlike the first test which checks `textContent.trim() === ''` (line 165). Cheap to strengthen with the same emptiness assertion.

findings.summary: No direct unit test for the plugin module itself, including the private `__rules__` lookup failure path
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws `markdown-it block rule not found` if the internal shape changes on a dependency bump. There is no packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.test.ts (glob of the view dir shows only preview/editor/commands/note-sync/remote-selection tests), so this brittle coupling is only exercised transitively; the throw path is never asserted.

findings.summary: Editor source pane still parses the lone `-` as a setext underline, so the two panes now disagree
findings.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200` builds the CodeMirror source pane with `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (lezer-markdown), which follows strict CommonMark and will keep highlighting `- 1\n  -` as a setext heading on the parent line. The preview `md` singleton (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48) now renders it as a nested empty bullet, so the source pane's syntax colouring and the rendered preview describe different documents for exactly the shape this change targets. Fix belongs either in the editor's markdown language config or in the design note that records the deviation.
searchedFor: grep markdown-it across repo (only notes/preview.ts + details-plugin.ts)

findings.summary: Deviation is broader than nested bullets: any top-level single-dash setext heading, and `*`/`+` empty bullets, change rendering for existing stored notes
findings.evidence:
The wrapper is keyed only on `state.parentType === 'paragraph'` and `isEmptyBulletLine` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:181-190), which is also true at top level. Existing note content of the form `Title
-` (a legal CommonMark h2) will now render as a paragraph plus an empty `<ul>`, and `foo
*` / `foo
+` now terminate the paragraph into an empty list where they previously stayed inline text (`breaks: true` soft break, preview.ts:18). No consumer of the shared `md` singleton (all NotePreview instances, editor.ts:117) was scoped away from this; docs/design/notes/notes.md:297 only documents that `---` and `=` underlines are untouched, not that single-dash top-level setext headings stop working.

findings.summary: `lheading` is now a hand-copied fork of markdown-it 14.x internals; upstream fixes to that rule will silently stop applying
findings.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:180) replaces the upstream rule with a full copy of `rules_block/lheading.mjs`, including a re-implementation of markdown-it's private `asciiTrim` (lines 17-23). Any upstream change to lheading (token shape, map handling, terminator semantics) is now invisible to this package, and nothing in CI pins the markdown-it version's rule body, so the fork can diverge without a test failing. Only notes consumes markdown-it (grep: preview.ts, details-plugin.ts), so the impact is contained to the notes preview.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` uses a catastrophically backtracking (quadratic) regex on attacker-controlled note text
findings.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is applied with `String.replace` to the whole setext-heading body at line 134-136 (`asciiTrim(state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false))`). The second alternative `[ws]+$` is not anchored at the start, so with the `g` flag the engine restarts at every index; for an interior whitespace run of length L that is NOT at the end of the string it greedily consumes the run, fails `$`, and backtracks one character at a time — O(L) per start index, O(L^2) overall. Vector: a workspace collaborator saves a note containing a setext heading whose paragraph line holds a long interior whitespace run, e.g. `"x" + " ".repeat(200000) + "x\n==="`. Note content lives in Yorkie and is rendered by every other member's `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165, synchronous `md.render` on the main thread with no timeout and no try/catch), so the stored note freezes each viewer's tab — a stored client-side DoS. Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` uses the native, linear `String.prototype.trim()` here, so this regex is a regression introduced by the diff; the comment on line 17 claiming it re-creates markdown-it's own `asciiTrim` does not change the backtracking behaviour. Fix: use `str.trim()` or split into two separately-anchored non-global replaces (`/^[ws]+/` and `/[ws]+$/`).

findings.summary: Silent-mode `return true` asserts a paragraph terminator without re-checking the conditions the non-silent `list` rule enforces, risking an uncaught markdown-it exception (blank preview) on crafted input
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` (lines 181-193) short-circuits with `return true` whenever `silent && parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)`, never delegating to `originalList`. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent` (line 32); it does not reproduce the stock list rule's non-silent rejections (`sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block guard, and the `listIndent` special case). If any caller invokes paragraph-terminator rules with `parentType === 'paragraph'` on a line the non-silent `list` rule would then refuse, markdown-it's block tokenizer can end up with no rule consuming the line and throws (`none of the block rules matched` / `block rule didn't increment state.line`); `NotePreview.render` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) has no try/catch, so the exception propagates out of render and the preview pane is left broken for anyone opening that note. I traced the two in-tree callers that set `parentType='paragraph'` (markdown-it's `paragraph` rule and the copied `lheading` at line 86), and both skip lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before invoking terminators, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence. Hardening: make the fast path `return originalList(...) || <empty-bullet check>` narrowed to conditions the non-silent rule accepts, rather than an unconditional `true`.

findings.summary: No test exercises adversarial/pathological input for the new block rules (long whitespace runs, deep or repeated empty-bullet nesting)
findings.evidence: The added tests (preview.test.ts:151-195) only cover the four happy-path shapes from the todo doc. Nothing renders a large or adversarial document through the new `lheading`/`list` replacements, so the quadratic `asciiTrim` behaviour and any parser-divergence crash would ship undetected. This does not by itself create a vulnerability, but it means the DoS surface introduced by the new rules is unmeasured.
searchedFor: Grep 'markdown-it|NotePreview' across **/*.{ts,tsx,json} — only packages/notes/src/view/* and harness.config.json
Glob packages/notes/src/view/*.ts for a dedicated plugin test file (none exists for list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts)

samples.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` uses a catastrophically backtracking (quadratic) regex on attacker-controlled note text
samples.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is applied with `String.replace` to the whole setext-heading body at line 134-136 (`asciiTrim(state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false))`). The second alternative `[ws]+$` is not anchored at the start, so with the `g` flag the engine restarts at every index; for an interior whitespace run of length L that is NOT at the end of the string it greedily consumes the run, fails `$`, and backtracks one character at a time — O(L) per start index, O(L^2) overall. Vector: a workspace collaborator saves a note containing a setext heading whose paragraph line holds a long interior whitespace run, e.g. `"x" + " ".repeat(200000) + "x\n==="`. Note content lives in Yorkie and is rendered by every other member's `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165, synchronous `md.render` on the main thread with no timeout and no try/catch), so the stored note freezes each viewer's tab — a stored client-side DoS. Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` uses the native, linear `String.prototype.trim()` here, so this regex is a regression introduced by the diff; the comment on line 17 claiming it re-creates markdown-it's own `asciiTrim` does not change the backtracking behaviour. Fix: use `str.trim()` or split into two separately-anchored non-global replaces (`/^[ws]+/` and `/[ws]+$/`).

samples.summary: Silent-mode `return true` asserts a paragraph terminator without re-checking the conditions the non-silent `list` rule enforces, risking an uncaught markdown-it exception (blank preview) on crafted input
samples.evidence: `wrappedList` (lines 181-193) short-circuits with `return true` whenever `silent && parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)`, never delegating to `originalList`. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent` (line 32); it does not reproduce the stock list rule's non-silent rejections (`sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block guard, and the `listIndent` special case). If any caller invokes paragraph-terminator rules with `parentType === 'paragraph'` on a line the non-silent `list` rule would then refuse, markdown-it's block tokenizer can end up with no rule consuming the line and throws (`none of the block rules matched` / `block rule didn't increment state.line`); `NotePreview.render` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) has no try/catch, so the exception propagates out of render and the preview pane is left broken for anyone opening that note. I traced the two in-tree callers that set `parentType='paragraph'` (markdown-it's `paragraph` rule and the copied `lheading` at line 86), and both skip lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before invoking terminators, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence. Hardening: make the fast path `return originalList(...) || <empty-bullet check>` narrowed to conditions the non-silent rule accepts, rather than an unconditional `true`.
